BREAKING: SWEET MAGNOLIAS has officially been cancelled by Netflix after five seasons, meaning there will be no Season 6 and the story of Serenity has officially come to an end. 

JoAnna Garcia Swisher, Brooke Elliott and Heather Headley led the series as Maddie, Dana Sue and Helen, three lifelong best friends navigating relationships, family and careers in the small South Carolina town. 

Season 5 premiered in June and ultimately became the final chapter, leaving several storylines open despite earlier hopes from the cast and creative team that the series could continue. 

There is at least one silver lining, with Netflix ordering a new drama titled LADIES OF THE HOUSE from SWEET MAGNOLIAS showrunner Sheryl J. Anderson and JoAnna Garcia Swisher. 

After five seasons of friendships, margarita nights and life in Serenity, SWEET MAGNOLIAS is officially saying goodbye to Netflix.

Ryan Murphy’s MONSTER franchise has now told four completely different true crime stories, and the critical reaction has varied wildly from season to season.

DAHMER: THE JEFFREY DAHMER STORY remains the highest rated season with 57%, while the newly released THE LIZZIE BORDEN STORY currently sits close behind at 50%.

THE LYLE AND ERIK MENENDEZ STORY holds a 47% critics score, putting it just behind the new Lizzie Borden chapter.

THE ED GEIN STORY remains the lowest rated season by a huge margin at just 22%, despite Charlie Hunnam leading the third installment.

Four seasons, four infamous cases and four very different reactions, but for now DAHMER still holds the strongest Rotten Tomatoes score in the MONSTER franchise.

MONSTER: THE LIZZIE BORDEN STORY has officially hit the No. 1 spot on Netflix just 12 hours after its release, giving the anthology an immediate monster sized debut.

Ella Beatty leads the fourth season as Lizzie Borden, marking the franchise’s first female centered story after seasons focused on Jeffrey Dahmer, the Menendez brothers and Ed Gein. 

Vicky Krieps stars as Bridget “Maggie” Sullivan alongside Charlie Hunnam, Rebecca Hall, Billie Lourd, Jessica Barden and Sarah Paulson in the eight episode season. 

The new chapter reimagines the infamous 1892 Borden murders through themes of repression, female rage and the mystery surrounding a woman who was tried and ultimately acquitted of killing her father and stepmother. 

MONSTER: THE LIZZIE BORDEN STORY is now streaming on Netflix, and reaching No. 1 within its first 12 hours is a huge start for the anthology’s blood red era.

Vicky Krieps and Ella Beatty celebrated the release of MONSTER: THE LIZZIE BORDEN STORY together as the new season officially began streaming on Netflix today. 

Beatty leads the fourth season as Lizzie Borden, while Krieps plays Bridget “Maggie” Sullivan, the Borden family maid whose relationship with Lizzie becomes one of the central parts of the story. 

The pair attended the New York premiere alongside Charlie Hunnam, Billie Lourd, Jessica Barden and other members of the cast before all eight episodes dropped on September 17. 

Their complicated relationship drives much of the new chapter, with the series exploring repression, desire and female rage while heavily dramatizing the infamous 1892 Borden murders. 

MONSTER: THE LIZZIE BORDEN STORY is now streaming on Netflix, and Vicky Krieps and Ella Beatty are officially at the center of the anthology’s blood red era.

Millie Bobby Brown and Jake Bongiovi have welcomed their second child through adoption, expanding their family just over a year after becoming parents for the first time. 

The couple adopted their first daughter in the summer of 2025 and have kept her identity completely private, choosing not to share her name or face publicly. 

Reports of baby number two emerged after Brown shared footage from a family trip to the Dolomites, where she could be seen carrying one child while Bongiovi appeared with another baby in a carrier. 

Brown has previously spoken openly about always wanting a large family and said adoption had been part of that dream since she was young. 

At just 22, Millie Bobby Brown is reportedly now a mother of two, beginning another completely new chapter of life with Jake Bongiovi.
